overview: This enum classifies each item by what it represents and how the game uses it.

None.simple: This marks an item slot with no item type.
None.technical: EGameItemType::None is the constructor default for FGameDataTableRow_Item and FGameDataTableRow_ShopLineup. UGameItemIconWidget::CanShowItem rejects it, and the shop category controller hides all sale lists when the selected tab carries it.

Money.technical: EGameItemType::Money is handled through user money instead of per-item stock. GameItem_GrantInitialItems adds the row amount with AddUserMoney, GameItem_SpendItem subtracts the count with AddUserMoney, and GameItem_GrantMaxPossession skips ordinary stock handling for it.

ShortStory.simple: This represents an unlockable short story.
ShortStory.technical: EGameItemType::ShortStory has a shop category tab and maps to the collection archive's Movies content. StoryLaunchHelpers resolves a ShortStory row id through Story_FindItemIdByVariableId_13022D0, and GamePhase_MainMenuStory marks the story seen when GameItem_HasStock reports ownership of the matching Item row.

Costume.simple: This represents an outfit for a character.
Costume.technical: EGameItemType::Costume resolves through the first CharacterVariation row whose Id_Item equals the Item row id. That variation supplies the full and thumbnail image names, GameItem_GetCharacterId walks back to the owning character, and collection and achievement code counts owned costume rows.

Title.simple: This represents a title for a player card.
Title.technical: EGameItemType::Title maps to the collection archive's Titles section, selects a label-only shop list, and is grouped with Nickname, Emblem, and Plate by the enum-order test from Title through Plate. GameItem_GetNameTextCore leaves its text id unchanged, and player-card helpers count owned title rows.

Nickname.simple: This represents a nickname for a player card.
Nickname.technical: EGameItemType::Nickname maps to the collection archive's Nicknames section and selects a two-line label shop list. GameItem_GetNameTextCore passes its text id through PlayerCard_MakeNicknameTextId, which applies the language-specific TOP and BOTTOM suffix rewrite.

Emblem.simple: This represents an emblem for a player card.
Emblem.technical: EGameItemType::Emblem maps to the collection archive's Emblems section and uses the Item row id as its image file name. Full and thumbnail image helpers return that id directly, and player-card helpers find owned emblems by Item.VariableId against PlayerCardEmblem rows.

Plate.simple: This represents a decoration plate for a player card.
Plate.technical: EGameItemType::Plate maps to the collection archive's DecorationPlates section and selects a label-only shop list. GameItemIconWidget resolves Item.VariableId against PlayerCardPlateDataTables and chooses either ImageFileName or ThumbnailImageFileName according to bShowThumbnail.

CursedTools.simple: This represents a cursed tool that a fighter can equip.
CursedTools.technical: EGameItemType::CursedTools maps to the CursedTools archive and battle-equipment tab. Image helpers use the Item row id directly, item description lookup follows Item.VariableId into EquipmentItemDataTable, and the vs-enemy equipment list filters ItemType values from CursedTools through Extras.

CursedObjects.simple: This represents a cursed object that a fighter can equip.
CursedObjects.technical: EGameItemType::CursedObjects maps to the CursedObjects archive and battle-equipment tab. Image helpers use the Item row id directly, item description lookup follows Item.VariableId into EquipmentItemDataTable, and the vs-enemy equipment list builds a dedicated CursedObjects tab.

Extras.simple: This represents a consumable battle item.
Extras.technical: EGameItemType::Extras maps to the Extras archive and battle-equipment tab, uses the Item row id as its image file name, and exposes its first equipment effect through BTL_ITEM_BUFF_MESSAGE_1000. UGameBattleExtrasItemWidget shows its icon when an equipped item resolves to this type, and UGameCharacterStatusController clears that equipment slot and calls ConsumeItem after applying the effect.

CustomVoice.simple: This represents an unlockable character voice.
CustomVoice.technical: EGameItemType::CustomVoice resolves Item.VariableId against CharacterCustomVoiceDataTables. GameItem_GetCharacterId returns the linked character, GameItem_GetNameTextCore uses ITM_CUSTOM_VOICE_1001 with CHARACTER_NAME and ITEM_NAME parameters, and the icon widget tints the background from Voice.Category and Voice.IndexType.

SituationOverviewPose.simple: This represents an unlockable presentation pose.
SituationOverviewPose.technical: EGameItemType::SituationOverviewPose resolves Item.VariableId against SituationOverviewPoseDataTables. GameItem_GetCharacterId finds the SituationOverview row containing that pose id, GameItem_GetNameTextCore uses ITM_SITUATION_OVERVIEW_POSE_1001, and the item icon uses the pose's ImageFileName or ThumbnailImageFileName according to bShowThumbnail.

StoryDemoMovie.simple: This represents an unlockable story demo movie.
StoryDemoMovie.technical: EGameItemType::StoryDemoMovie maps to the collection archive's Movies section and receives a shop category tab. UGameItemIconWidget treats it as showable and gives it a category sprite, while GameShopLotteryLineup_IsPreviewable places it with the non-previewable item types.

Character.simple: This is the enum slot named for character items.
Character.technical: EGameItemType::Character is declared after StoryDemoMovie and before Invalid. No consumer using this enumerator appears in the available Source, so its gameplay handling cannot be traced from static evidence.

Invalid.simple: This marks an item type that could not be resolved.
Invalid.technical: EGameItemType::Invalid is used as the sentinel when GameShop_HasNewLineupOfType cannot resolve an Item row for a lineup set. That value is then compared with the tab's CategoryType while checking shop new flags.

notes: The enum is a uint8 with sequential declared members through Character and an explicit invalid sentinel at the end.
Several consumers test enum order. GameManager groups Title through Plate as player-card items, and the vs-enemy equipment list groups CursedTools through Extras.
The supplied table explanations report no ItemDataTable rows using StoryDemoMovie or Character. Their source-level consumers are still listed here where a consumer switch exists.
UI switches commonly fall through to no icon, no preview, or no overlay for types they do not handle. The behavior is described per member only where a matching branch was found.
